label: <DEL> step of length-3 sequences, gated by first/last original token identity
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit (0.03% of steps). 92% of activation mass is on the <DEL> delimiter step, almost entirely when L=3 (t=3, rate 2% vs 0.03% base; 88% of mass); a small remainder is on the <DEL> at L=4 and on z/k inputs at t=3 in longer sequences. Never fires in the copy phase. Within L=3 delimiters, only about 12% fire; whether it fires depends on token identity: first original token (n is strongest, 8.5x lift, and leads the top examples; also f,u,i,j,h,v,b,g) and the last original token just before <DEL> (r strongest; also y,x,l,2,3,h,d). Combining delimiter-at-L=3 with both token sets gives dev P 0.77 / R 0.56 / F1 0.65 / mass recall 0.71. The largest activations are n-initial sequences ending in r/x/y. The token dependence looks graded and additive rather than a clean set rule, so the token lists are an approximation. It does not fire on original-phase letters other than z/k, on digit-heavy sequences (n_digits>=2), or at any copy step.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: n, f, u, i, v, h; least: 1, q, z, 2) and the previous input (most: r, y, 2, 3, l, x; least: a, g, f, b); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, L=3 & t=3, L=3.
